known_failures.evidence: Every failing case: the client completed the handshake (outcome success, TLS 1.3 state Complete) instead of terminating.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 5.1: a zero-length handshake record must end the connection with unexpected_message. The record layer accepts it, so the handshake completes.

known_failures.evidence: Every failing case: the client completed the handshake (outcome success, TLS 1.3 state Complete) instead of terminating.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.2: an extension not allowed in the message it appears in must abort the handshake with illegal_parameter. ServerHello extension handling ignores a heartbeat extension that the ClientHello did not offer.

known_failures.evidence: Client outcome handshake-error with BR_ERR_UNEXPECTED after the handshake completed, in every case. The suite fails the cases where it expects illegal_parameter.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.6.3: an unknown request_update value must end the connection with illegal_parameter. Certainly rejects every post-handshake KeyUpdate as unexpected, so it neither updates keys nor distinguishes invalid values. The verdict is partial because some cases accept closure in any form.

known_failures.evidence: Client outcome handshake-error with BR_ERR_UNEXPECTED after the handshake completed, in every case; the suite never received the expected KeyUpdate.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.6.3: a receiver of update_requested must answer with its own KeyUpdate. KeyUpdate is mandatory to implement; src/tls13_handshake.c treats it as a connection close instead.

known_failures.evidence: Every failing case: the client completed the handshake (outcome success, TLS 1.3 state Complete) instead of terminating.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.3.1: the client must reject forbidden extensions in EncryptedExtensions with illegal_parameter. The EncryptedExtensions parser skips extensions it does not use without checking that they are permitted there.

known_failures.evidence: Every failing case: the client completed the handshake (outcome success, TLS 1.3 state Complete) instead of terminating.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.3.1: the client must reject forbidden extensions in EncryptedExtensions with illegal_parameter. A supported_versions extension there is accepted.

known_failures.evidence: Every failing case: the client completed the handshake without sending Certificate after a CertificateRequest; the suite received Finished directly (outcome success, TLS 1.3 state Complete).
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.4.2: when the server requests client authentication and no certificate is available, the client must send a Certificate message with no certificates before Finished. src/tls13_handshake.c notes the CertificateRequest and defers the empty Certificate reply. Client certificates themselves are out of scope; the empty reply is not.

known_failures.evidence: Client outcome handshake-error with BR_ERR_UNEXPECTED after the handshake completed, in every case.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.6.3: a receiver of KeyUpdate must update its receiving keys and keep exchanging data. Certainly closes the connection instead of rekeying.

known_failures.evidence: Every failing case: the client completed the handshake (outcome success, TLS 1.3 state Complete) instead of terminating.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 4.2: an extension response with no matching request must abort the handshake with unsupported_extension. Unsolicited extensions are ignored.

known_failures.evidence: Discovery-evaluated: the suite's scan of the ClientHello found no secp256r1 key share or supported group; X25519 is the only group offered. No connection is made for this verdict.
known_failures.explanation: RFC 8446 section 9.1: a TLS-compliant application must support key exchange with secp256r1. The TLS 1.3 handshake implements X25519 only, which also leaves the suite's HelloRetryRequest templates inapplicable.
